Admission Plasma Glucose Requirement
data.description: Plasma glucose range required on Day 1 of each admission; otherwise admission rescheduled
data.text: Admission can be rescheduled if PG level is not 90 to 250 mg/dL on Day 1.

data.name: Hypoglycemia Induction Target (Insulin Infusion Stop)
data.description: Target plasma glucose threshold to stop insulin infusion and proceed to dosing
data.text: Insulin infusion is stopped once bedside PG is <60 mg/dL; approximately 5 minutes later study drug is administered (Time = 0 min).

data.name: Hypoglycemia Symptom Assessment Threshold
data.description: Plasma glucose threshold defining the 'during hypoglycemia induction' assessment time point
data.text: During hypoglycemia induction will be when PG ≤75 mg/dL.

data.name: Bedside PG Monitoring Frequency Condition
data.description: Monitoring frequency depends on bedside plasma glucose level
data.text: Bedside PG monitoring will be conducted no more than 10 minutes apart while bedside PG is ≥90 mg/dL and no more than 5 minutes apart when bedside PG is <90 mg/dL.

data.name: Interim Safety Review Condition (First 6 Patients)
data.description: Safety data review gate before dosing remaining patients
data.text: Safety data will be reviewed after the first 6 patients (regardless of type of diabetes) are administered LY900018 in Period 2; the investigator and Lilly CRP/scientist will review AEs, SAEs, vital signs, ECGs, and safety laboratory tests after these patients complete Period 2 Day 1. If no clinically significant safety findings for treatment or study procedure are noted, the remaining patients will be dosed.

data.name: Insufficient Response to Glucagon Administration
data.description: Condition triggering rescue procedures per Section 9.2.4
data.text: Procedures for insufficient response to glucagon administration are to be followed (Section 9.2.4).

data.name: Treatment-Emergent ADA at Follow-up
data.description: Immunogenicity condition triggering additional follow-up visits
data.text: Patients with TE ADA at follow-up/ED will undergo additional follow-up; immunogenicity samples should be collected every 12 weeks (84±7 days) until the titer returns to baseline (within a single 2-fold dilution of the baseline titer) or until 1 year after the last dose of study treatment.

data.name: Insulin Regimen Acceptability
data.description: Pre-procedure review of insulin regimen before hypoglycemia induction
data.text: Review patients' insulin regimens to confirm acceptability to undergo the procedure to induce hypoglycemia.

data.name: Discharge Readiness Condition
data.description: Conditions for discharge from CRU after dosing
data.text: Patient may be discharged 6 hours after glucagon administration after receiving a carbohydrate-rich meal and the investigator ensuring the patient's PG is stable; a patient may remain inpatient at the CRU at the discretion of the investigator.

data.name: Non-inferiority Decision Criterion
data.description: Primary statistical success criterion
data.text: Non-inferiority of LY900018 will be declared if the upper limit of the 2-sided 95% CI constructed on the difference in percentage (IMG - LY900018) is less than the non-inferiority margin of 10%.

data.name: Sample Size / Completer Requirement
data.description: Enrollment and completion condition governing replacement
data.text: Seventy five patients may be enrolled in order to have at least 66 patients (at least 30 patients with T1DM and T2DM, respectively) complete both periods with evaluable primary outcome; replacement should not occur beyond 75 patients enrolled if it is expected to have at least 66 patients complete the study.

data.name: Pregnancy Test Requirement
data.description: Testing condition for women of childbearing potential
data.text: Serum pregnancy test will be performed at screening; urine pregnancy test will be performed at every admission period and follow-up visit if applicable.

data.name: FSH Confirmation Condition
data.description: FSH testing only when needed
data.text: FSH (female patients only) when needed to confirm postmenopausal status.

data.name: Inadvertently Enrolled Patient Continuation Condition
data.description: Agreement requirement to allow continuation of patient who did not meet enrollment criteria
data.text: A discussion must occur between the Lilly CP/CRP and the investigator to determine if the patient may continue; if both agree it is medically appropriate, the investigator must obtain documented approval from the Lilly CP/CRP to continue with or without continued treatment with investigational product.

data.name: Screening to Period 1 Transition
data.text: Patients undergo screening within 28 days prior to enrollment (Days -28 to -2); prior to study drug administration on Period 1 Day 1, eligible patients are randomly assigned to a treatment sequence (LY900018 then IMG, or IMG then LY900018).

data.name: Period 1 to Washout Transition
data.text: After single-dose administration and up to 4 hours of PK/PD sampling and at least 6 hours in the CRU, patients are discharged and enter a washout period of 3 to 14 days.

data.name: Washout to Period 2 Transition (Crossover)
data.text: After a washout of 3 to 14 days, patients are re-admitted on Day -1 and crossover to the alternate treatment in Period 2; procedures in Period 2 will occur at approximately the same time as those in Period 1.

data.name: Period 2 to Follow-up Transition
data.text: Patients return for a follow-up visit within 28±2 days (26 to 30 days) after the last study treatment.

data.name: Follow-up to Additional TE ADA Follow-up Transition
data.text: Patients with treatment-emergent antidrug antibodies at the follow-up/ED visit transition to additional immunogenicity follow-up every 12 weeks (84±7 days) until titer returns to baseline or 1 year after last dose.

data.name: Safety Gate Before Dosing Remaining Patients
data.text: The remaining patients will be dosed only after review and confirmation of safety data from the first 6 patients who complete Period 2 Day 1 (no clinically significant safety findings for treatment or study procedure).

data.name: Rescheduling of Admission for Out-of-Range Plasma Glucose
data.text: Admission can be rescheduled if PG level is not 90 to 250 mg/dL on Day 1, delaying hypoglycemia induction and study treatment administration.

data.name: Insulin Infusion Stop Rule
data.text: Insulin infusion to induce hypoglycemia is stopped once bedside PG is <60 mg/dL; approximately 5 minutes later study drug is administered.

data.name: Rescue for Insufficient Glucagon Response
data.text: Procedures for insufficient response to glucagon administration will be followed (Section 9.2.4); a carbohydrate-rich meal and, if needed, a prandial insulin dose are administered after completion of PK sampling with investigator confirmation of stable PG.

data.name: Discontinuation for Enrollment in Other Research
data.text: Patients will be discontinued for enrollment in any other clinical study involving an investigational product or any other type of medical research judged not to be scientifically or medically compatible with this study.

data.name: Discontinuation for Medical/Safety/Regulatory Reasons
data.text: Patients will be discontinued if participation in the study needs to be stopped for medical, safety, regulatory, or other reasons consistent with applicable laws, regulations, and good clinical practice.

data.name: Discontinuation by Investigator Decision
data.text: The investigator decides that the patient should be discontinued from the study for any reason. If this decision is made because of an AE, SAE, or a severe hypoglycemia event, appropriate measures are to be taken and Lilly or its designee is to be alerted.

data.name: Discontinuation by Patient Decision
data.text: The patient, or legal representative, requests to be withdrawn from the study.

data.name: Discontinuation of Inadvertently Enrolled Patients
data.text: If a patient who did not meet enrollment criteria was inadvertently enrolled, the patient is discontinued unless the Lilly CP/CRP and investigator agree and documented approval is obtained to continue with or without continued treatment with investigational product.

data.name: Study-Level Termination for Safety
data.text: Following the review of the safety data from the first 6 patients to complete Period 2 Day 1, the study will be stopped if deemed necessary for patient safety in the opinion of the investigator and sponsor.

data.name: Early Discontinuation (ED) Visit
data.description: Patients discontinuing from the study prematurely for any reason must complete AE and follow-up procedures as shown in the Schedule of Activities, including the Follow-up/ED visit (within 28±2 days after last study treatment).

data.name: Study Completion
data.description: Completion of both treatment periods with evaluable primary outcome plus the follow-up visit 26 to 30 days (28±2 days) after the last study treatment; patients with TE ADA complete additional immunogenicity follow-up until titer returns to baseline or 1 year after last dose.

data.name: Lost to Follow-up
data.description: A patient will be considered lost to follow-up if he or she repeatedly fails to return for scheduled visits and is unable to be contacted by the study site after diligent attempts.

data.name: Discontinuation of the Study (Sponsor/Investigator)
data.description: The study will be stopped if deemed necessary for patient safety in the opinion of the investigator and sponsor following the safety review of the first 6 patients completing Period 2 Day 1.

data.name: Exit Due to Ineligibility (Inadvertent Enrollment)
data.description: Patients identified as not meeting enrollment criteria who were inadvertently enrolled are discontinued unless documented approval from the Lilly CP/CRP permits continuation; such patients may be replaced up to a maximum of 75 enrolled.

data.name: Admission Eligibility Decision (Plasma Glucose)
data.description: At each period Day 1, determine whether PG is 90 to 250 mg/dL and insulin regimen is acceptable; otherwise reschedule admission.

data.name: Insulin Infusion Stop / Dosing Decision
data.description: During hypoglycemia induction, bedside PG monitoring determines when PG <60 mg/dL, triggering infusion stop and study treatment administration approximately 5 minutes later (Time = 0 min).

data.name: Interim Safety Review Decision After First 6 Patients
data.description: After the first 6 patients complete Period 2 Day 1, the investigator and Lilly CRP/scientist decide whether to dose the remaining patients or stop the study for patient safety.

data.name: Glucagon Response Assessment Decision
data.description: Post glucagon administration, assess response; if insufficient response, follow rescue procedures (Section 9.2.4).

data.name: Discharge Decision
data.description: At 6 hours after glucagon administration, decide whether the patient may be discharged following a carbohydrate-rich meal and stable PG, or remain inpatient at the investigator's discretion.

data.name: Immunogenicity Follow-up Decision
data.description: At the follow-up/ED visit, determine TE ADA status; if positive, schedule additional samples every 12 weeks (84±7 days) until titer returns to baseline or 1 year after last dose.

data.name: Primary Non-inferiority Analysis Decision
data.description: Primary analysis comparing treatment success percentages; non-inferiority declared if upper limit of 2-sided 95% CI for (IMG - LY900018) is less than 10%.

data.name: Patient Replacement Decision
data.description: If a patient discontinues before completing both periods with evaluable primary outcome, decide on replacement (not beyond 75 patients enrolled).
